5. Termination of Agreement: The NDA will outline circumstances under which either party can terminate the agreement, such as breach of the agreement by the other party, expiration of the agreement, or mutual agreement between the parties.
6. Governing Law: The NDA will usually state which jurisdiction's laws apply to any disputes arising out of the agreement.
7. Counterparts: The NDA may allow multiple counterparts to be signed, meaning that each party can sign an original copy and then have the other party sign a copy, creating two identical copies.
8. Attorneys' Fees: In case of a dispute over the interpretation or enforcement of the NDA, the prevailing party may be entitled to recover its attorneys' fees.
9. Waiver of Rights: The NDA may waive the right of either party to seek injunctive relief against the other party for alleged violations of the agreement.
